reviews.comment: Worst prof I've ever had at A&M. Chose to have a horrible schedule the following semester just so I wouldn't have him again. He likes to change the requirements for major projects with 0 notice and only stopped when students started contacting his superiors about it . Don't get him started if someone accidentally uses the word "like".
Bring ear plugs and maybe you can hear yourself think in this class.

Projects in this class were fun, but there were NEVER any clear or posted instructions, they were graded arbitrarily, and class was spent entirely giving "feedback" that was subjective, pretentious, and often rude. He would tear apart student's work without even asking why they made a given creative choice. Learned nothing, take ANY other prof.

He's sort of the stereotypical professor you see in movies. Lectures were hard to get through but he's extremely knowledgeable if you get past the large vocabulary he loves to flaunt. Wants his students to succeed and get something out of the class. Open-note/internet exams. Two projects, one assignment, and a quiz due each week. Would recommend!

Lectures are basically pointless because he just talks about himself the whole time and rambles. As long as you copy notes on the slides and use the textbooks for the open note exams, you will be fine. Tests are somewhat challenging but he gives us 2 projects with assignments each week that boosts your grade. Overall is a doable class.

gives out projects with no clear instructions, grades them unfairly, gives live feedback in class that is often embarrassing and rude, does not teach during class time despite mandatory attendance. i dreaded this class with a passion. bruder is not an educator equipped to teach this class and it really affected my grade. honestly a trash course

Kurt Bruder is the worst educator I have ever had. His inflated ego, flawed grading practices, and disregard for fairness contradict the core values of academic integrity at A&M. DO NOT TAKE THIS PROFESSOR. You will not get a quality education in his course. I recommend literally anyone else.

(I could write much more - I only have 350 characters)

This was an interesting class but Bruder didn't teach us anything. Attendance is mandatory but all he does in class is roast students and their work. Classes are extremely boring. You have to figure out all the assignments on your own because he doesn't teach how to do them and changes the requirements in class the day before they're due.

Lectures not very helpful. He'd ramble about thing then skip through the important slides and say "you can read about this in the textbook."  Quizzes & exams are all open note. 2 projects during the semester w/ assignments due each week. Assignments not hard & were graded easily by TA but instructions were often confusing & lectures were unhelpful.

The class itself isn't difficult, he just tends to over explain and overcomplicate the assignments. He relies on students volunteering their assignments to be picked apart in class and he is very condescending. I can tell he is passionate about what the class teaches but he makes the class very anxiety inducing.

This professor is overall very inconsiderate. He will use your work in class to basically embarrass you and make you feel awkward. He tries to explain projects but it never makes sense. SUPER TOUGH GRADER! I enjoy this class but I would recommend another professor.
reviews.ratingTags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Not only does he expect you to come to class but does not teach anything, he only forces u to show your homework and projects to the class and then gives you harsh feedback that it incredibly embarrassing. He makes students feel super anxious due to his methods. He also takes forever to grade assignments and doesn't spend class time explaining them

Extremely unorganized, rude, unhelpful, and always has to reexplain himself. It seems like he doesn't know how to talk to students, and he makes people feel too uncomfortable to even volunteer in his class. I tried to give him the benefit if the doubt but when he started to give unfair grades, it really started to rub me the wrong way.

This professor was brand new. He came in using an old professors lectures and quiz's, but had us use the wrong textbook. Nothing matched up and when I realized that this was why we were doing so bad on the first couple of quiz's he got mad at me. He finally fixed the slides, but did not let us retake or drop the quiz's we all failed.

He is extremely unorganized and is extremely bad at using technology for someone teaching a technology class. He overcomplicates things almost every time he talks. He gave extremely harsh (and oftentimes rude or embarrassing) feedback to students he selected to show their work. Although I finished the class with a 100, it was an unenjoyable class.

I had professor Bruder for his very first class at A&M. He really is a sweet man and wants to get to know everyone, he just isn't as organized as I think he would like to be (this may be different as he adjusts to a new place).  HOWEVER, his exams are open note and the project is worth a big part of yvour grade which helped alot.
Very unorganized course. No clear grading criteria or due dates. Always changed up assignments last minute. Rude and unfiltered.

The course was very unorganized and the lectures were difficult to understand. Thankfully his exams were open note/book which helped me. Lots of in-class projects that were easy just get a good group. The group project was with 9 people, he split us up by last name going down the class roster and didn't give much direction on what was expected.

This was his first semester at A&M, he was practically thrown in a week before classes started and this class was extremely unorganized. He used a previous professor's slides which made it hard to follow and he was confusing during his lectures, but he did make his exams open book/note which SAVED me. The TA was the best and our saving grace.

*Rating for 230, which isn't an option* 

Although I'm finishing Dr. Bruder's class with a 100, this class was a circus. Nothing has clear criteria and be prepared to grow tough skin because he gives brutally honest feedback even if it comes across as offensive (hence his name). Easy class, but very difficult to follow.

This course has weekly quizzes and in-class assignments that contribute to a majority of your overall grade. I would necessarily say this class is overly difficult but he does not teach at all. all of the tests & quizzes were open note which saved me. your grade in this class is based on how well you can google

Yes, it was his first semester at A&M, but despite relying on previous prof's syllabus & Canvas page, it was still very unorganized. Lectures did not pertain to class content at all, so having an open-book test saved me. Completely skipped stats/math section in class. TA graded everything & was the lifeline for students. Would recommend avoiding.

Dr. Bruder has a wide array of skills that he's not afraid to make known or brag about. While he comes off as self righteous sometimes, he can be quite nice if you put in the work and it shows. He likes to hear his own voice during lectures and critiques brutally honest in presentations. He's not afraid to correct something that seems misaligned.
The class is easy as all the exams are open note and on your computer. However, this professor is highly unorganized, and good luck ever getting him to respond to an email. The TA carried this class.

It's definitely not a difficult class by any means, the tests are online, open book and open note. The quizzes are easy and the in class work is easy if you have a good group. He is very confusing to listen to and condescending if you don't answer a question how he wants you to. If you can avoid interaction with him, then it's an easy class.

The class is unorganized, but this was his first semester at A&M, so that is understandable. The concepts taught in class should be super easy, but are often overcomplicated. If possible, I would try to avoid this professor. Quizzes are pretty easy though, and tests are open book. Research assignments take time, but are pretty straight forward.

He was hired right before classes began and had little time to prepare syllabi/curriculums this semester. Taking that into consideration, I think he is doing a good job. He has been accommodating with any course issues. I think it would take genuine talent to fail this class. If you do the readings and follow assignment rubrics you'll be just fine.

Please avoid this prof at all costs! His lectures are extremely boring. He goes off topic and talks in a way that overcomplicates things. Tests were open note, online, in class. Tests were also multiple choice and short answer. Syllabus was inaccurate at the beginning. Also, a lot of online quizzes and research assignments.
